subject.title: [Feature]: REST endpoint for session management in HTTP API integrations

question: Should OpenClaw expose dedicated /v1/sessions/* REST management endpoints for HTTP integrations, expand the default-off admin HTTP RPC plugin to include session methods, or keep these controls on WebSocket/plugin surfaces only?
rationale: The backend capability exists, but exposing mutating session controls over authenticated HTTP changes OpenClaw's public control-plane and security boundary.

options.title: Dedicated REST session API
options.body: Add narrow /v1/sessions/* endpoints over the existing session handlers with explicit auth, scope, reserved-key, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Admin RPC only
options.body: Extend the default-off admin HTTP RPC plugin allowlist for session methods instead of adding first-class OpenAI-compatible REST routes.

options.title: Keep current surfaces
options.body: Leave session mutation on WebSocket/plugin APIs and document HTTP integrations as unsupported for these controls.

recommendation.title: Dedicated REST session API
recommendation.body: Add narrow /v1/sessions/* endpoints over the existing session handlers with explicit auth, scope, reserved-key, docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent history on the OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint and Gateway method-scope authorization surface.
